transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

With no lights or response at all, start with the power supply rather than the door lock or motor. The usual causes are the wall socket/switch or plug fuse, then the machine’s lead or internal mains filter; the control board is possible but comes later. With the machine switched off, try a known-working appliance in the same socket and check that any socket switch or fused spur is on. Do not remove any machine covers. Does the other appliance work there?
yeah the kettle works in the other sockets in the kitchen. the washing machine is built in behind a cupboard door tho so i cant get to the plug

The kettle working in other kitchen sockets shows the kitchen supply is broadly live, but it does not prove the washing machine’s own hidden socket is live. Built-in machines are often fed through a separate switched fused spur or an accessible isolator. If its switch is on and the machine remains completely dead, the leading possibilities become an internal mains filter/incoming connection, with the control board power supply less likely; that will need access by an appliance engineer.
sorry whats a spur? is that a switch somewhere? i dont really know what im looking for

Yes — a fused spur is usually a small fixed wall switch, often with a little pull-out fuse holder below or beside the switch. It may be labelled “washing machine”, but often is not; for a built-in machine it can be in the next cupboard, under/above the worktop, or on the kitchen wall. Don’t remove the fuse or take any panels off. Have a look for that switch and check whether it is set to ON; if you cannot find one, an engineer will need to access the appliance socket safely.
ok i had a look and theres a row of switches above the worktop. one says washer and its OFF. my flatmate must of switched it off when she was cleaning. should i turn it on?

Yes — turn the switch labelled “washer” to ON. That is the appliance’s isolator switch, so it is intended to be used for this. Then check whether the machine has any lights or responds to its power button. If it comes back on, the machine itself was simply isolated; if it remains completely dead, leave the switch on and it will need an engineer to access and test the hidden supply and internal power components.
ok i turned it on and the machine lights up now and works! thanks

That suggests it was simply switched off at the washer isolator, not a fault with the machine. Leaving that switch on should prevent the same issue; it is worth letting your flatmate know which switch feeds the washer. Is there anything else you need help with?
